risks.blocker: fully settled independent 48/50V hot faults lack completed log and waveform engineering review
risks.next_evidence: bench-verify OC delay and SR/Lr peaks on a physical sample; confirm real Lr saturation at the 101A fault peak.  The PR #21 soft-start question is closed: the fault is now injected after V(ss) reaches 3.982 V (5.045 V at 48 V, 5.045 V at 50 V), not during the 0.5 mV/us ramp.  The 50V 296.928us stall is numerical (smooth 3 V/us dead state, LTE-driven) -- standby cannot close it because tSTBY_DET is 7.5 ms -- and the prefix is accepted because every stress event ends before 215us.  PR #20's documented SOLVER_DIAGNOSTIC is now run: same circuit, trtol 7->1 and abstol 1e-12->1e-13 over 0..220us moves the I(Lr) peak by -0.16 % (-0.163 A), the SR forward peak by +0.002 % and the trip by -81 ns, so the prefix peaks are not a single-solver artifact.  The 48 V control (base run passed the strict log pre-check) moves the same peaks by -0.420 % and -0.411 %: both cases move down under tightening, so the direction is conservative, but the magnitude is sub-percent, not 0.1 %.  The stall itself is still unresolved and no number here is hardware evidence.  Closing F01 now also requires an independent engineering waveform review: hotfault_engineering_gate accepts a case only when hotfault_<case>_engineering_review.json is signed and digest-matched to the current deck, log and waveform data, not when the log pre-check passes

ELE-09 ruled out a short-window artifact (22 periods 0.4986 W vs 133 aligned 0.4921 W, sem 0.050 W) and the deck is now exhausted: no un-inventoried dissipative element can hold 0.49 W (Cin ESR 0.61 mW measured, Cbt carries no charge).  Remaining candidates are the port reading (~2 mV of mean Vout) and the behavioral-SR channel/diode split; measured across the four 100 A steps the SR body-diode term moves 118 W/V against the port's 200 W/V, so 1 mV of Vout is worth 0.12 W -- the 0.49 W gap is 2.1 mV, the same order.  The fixed-current legs give 102 W/V as well, so the coupling is to Vout and not to the load current.  Do not relax 0.2 W

the aligned 133-period window confirms the 0.698 W closure is stable (sem 0.050 W); ELE-09's inventory audit leaves only port and numerical candidates, and re-integrating the same samples is falsified (0.80 % within a raw against 86 % across steps).  More step reduction is falsified as well: with the load replaced by a constant-current sink the 0.5 ns leg still settles 15.1 mV above 5 ns and keeps 98.9 % of the resistive 5->0.5 ns endpoint difference, so the four runs sit at different operating points and the model's own V(out) moves with the step.  The sink is faithful (its 5 ns leg matches the resistive one to 0.3 %) but pins the current, not V(out) -- its own window drift is 4.7 mV.  Only a closed V(out) loop can pin the operating point, and that is a different deck; do not relax 0.2 W
